products.name: Peak Design Travel Tripod (Carbon Fiber)
products.query: Peak Design Travel Tripod carbon fiber
products.matchName: Peak Design Travel Tripod Carbon Fiber
products.summary: A five-section carbon tripod that folds to about 15.5 in, reaches 51.25 in with the column down and carries 20 lb. It is the pick when the tripod has to ride in a bag every day and still hold a full-frame body with a telephoto.
products.renterNote: Full-frame and mirrorless shooters up to a 70-200mm class lens who fly or hike with the tripod. Key caveat: the built-in ball head is the weak point owners mention, and it costs premium money.
pros: Folds to about 15.5 in and a water-bottle diameter, so it fits a bag pocket
20 lb rated load and 51.25 in column-down height are strong for the size
All five leg sections latch or release together with one hand
cons: Built-in ball head and column lock are hard to tighten firmly, per a PetaPixel owner
Premium-tier price, and a forum owner reported a leg coming off on the road

specs.Weight: 2.81 lb (1.27 kg), carbon fiber version, per retailer listings of the maker spec
specs.Head: Built-in compact ball head, single adjustment ring
specs.Plate: Peak Design standard plate; Arca-type plates work per retailer listings

products.scoreNote: 20 lb load and 51 in column-down height in a 15.5 in fold; thin lower legs and a fiddly built-in head hold back stability, and the price holds back value.
products.amazonTitle: Peak Design Travel Tripod, Carbon Fiber, Compact Design, Quick Setup and Takedown, Pro-Level Stability, Ergonomic Ball Head, Compact and Portable Travel Tripod for Camera and Phone, 20 lb Capacity

praise: Collapses small without a huge circumference, so it goes in checked luggage or a backpack
Legs are quick to set up and extremely stable once everything is locked
Durable: Pack Hacker's team reports four-plus years of weekly use with only a small adjuster fragment breaking off
complaints: Ball head and center column lock are hard to tighten securely
Expensive for what it is; one forum owner had a leg come off while traveling
Not something to trust in strong wind on exposed ground

sources.title: PetaPixel: My Experience with the Peak Design Travel Tripod
Fred Miranda forum: Peak Design issues
Pack Hacker: The Best Travel Tripod (long-term use)

ownerQuotes.quote: The legs are nice. Like really, really, really, nice. My favorite part is that I can easily latch and unlatch all of the legs at once with one hand, which makes setting up the tripod a breeze.
I wouldn't want to depend on it in 20 MPH winds on top of a glacier, but I can't think of any other travel tripod I would either.
But when I spun the knob to lock the column I never felt super confident that it would be tight enough.
I am out of town and went to use it an one of the legs came off.
we've been using the carbon fiber version of the Peak Design Travel Tripod for over four years and use it multiple times per week.

products.weak: Pack Hacker lists 3.432 lb / 1.56 kg for the carbon version, which matches the aluminum spec elsewhere; I used 2.81 lb from retailer listings of the maker spec (could not open the collapsed Specs tab on peakdesign.com). Matt Purciel recommends the Aluminum version, so 2-page evidence is at family level.

products.name: Sirui Traveler 5C Carbon Fiber Tripod
products.summary: A 0.85 kg carbon tripod with five sections and twist locks that folds to about 13 in and reaches 54.3 in with the column raised. It suits a small mirrorless kit and a daypack.
products.renterNote: Mirrorless or crop-sensor shooters with a body and a standard zoom who want the lightest tripod in the bag. Key caveat: the 8.8 lb (4 kg) rating and a wobbly raised column limit it with a long telephoto or in wind.
pros: About 1.9 lb and a 13 in fold, so it disappears into a backpack
Five-section twist locks and a removable column that allows low shots
Arca Swiss-style quick-release plate on the included ball head per the Amazon listing
cons: TechGearLab found it not confidence-inspiring in wind with the column fully raised
The single-knob ball head is the weak point, per owners and reviewers

specs.Max height (center column down): About 40 in (102.5 cm), per retailer listings (not on a maker page I could open)
specs.Weight: 0.85 kg (1.87 lb) per First Quadcopter; listings range 850 to 895 g
specs.Head: Included ball head, single knob for friction and lock (25 mm ball)
specs.Plate: Arca Swiss compatible per the Amazon listing title

products.scoreNote: Lightest and smallest of the three with a very low entry cost for carbon; the 4 kg rating, wobbly raised column and basic head cap stability and height.
products.amazonTitle: Sirui Compact Traveler 5C Tripod 54.3 inches Lightweight Carbon Fiber Travel Tripod for Camera with 360° Panorama Ball Head for Arca Swiss Quick Release Plate, Max Load 8.8lbs

praise: Amazingly small and light; fits inside a backpack for a two-week trip
Lightweight, sturdy for mirrorless kits and fine for product and studio work
Handled mud and field conditions without damage
complaints: 4 kg capacity is a huge limitation when fully extended; one owner returned it with an A7 III and 24-70mm
Center column shaky when fully extended; a sandbag or hanging bag helps
Ball head is the most limiting part; some owners swap it

sources.title: Fred Miranda forum: Anyone Using the Sirui 5C?
First Quadcopter: SIRUI Traveler 5C review and reader comments

ownerQuotes.quote: It is an amazingly small tripod that fits inside of my backpack which was ideal for a two week trip to the UK and France.
The ballhead works but is probably the most limiting aspect.
Recently bought it and had to return it. The weight capacity is 4kg which is a huge limitation when fully extended.
I've had this tripod for about a year and I love it!
when we fully extended the center column to its max height (54.3 inches), the SIRUI wasn't very confidence-inspiring in the wind.

products.weak: No maker (sirui.com) page opened; specs from First Quadcopter, TechGearLab and AU/EU retailer listings, which disagree slightly (weight 850-895 g, one German retailer says 6 kg load). Column-down height (about 102.5 cm) is retailer-only. Owner count includes 2 commenter owners on First Quadcopter and 2 Fred Miranda posters. Already a pick in best-travel-tripod-for-mirrorless-camera.

products.name: 3 Legged Thing Winston 2.0 Carbon Fibre Tripod Kit
products.query: 3 Legged Thing Winston 2.0 carbon fibre tripod kit
products.matchName: 3 Legged Thing Winston 2.0 Kit Carbon Fibre Tripod
products.summary: A big three-section carbon tripod rated to 88 lb at its narrowest leg angle, with 55.5 in of height without the column and 72.8 in with it. It is the stable pick for long lenses, landscapes and studio work when weight does not matter.
products.renterNote: DSLR and mirrorless shooters with 70-200mm to 600mm lenses, or anyone who wants a rock-solid base at eye level. Key caveat: it folds to 24 in and weighs 3.8 lb without the head, so it is not a carry-on tripod.
pros: 40 kg (88 lb) rated load at the 23 degree leg angle, with 25 kg at 55 degrees
55.5 in without the center column and 72.8 in with it, so tall users reach eye level
Legs detach into a monopod, and the kit adds an AirHed Pro ball head with an Arca-Swiss compatible plate
cons: Folded length is 24 in, and The Phoblographer found it larger than they would want for travel
Owners report the section couplings can take on water when submerged; one reviewer had ball head locking close calls

specs.Weight: 3.8 lb (1.73 kg) for the tripod system, per 3 Legged Thing
specs.Max load: 88 lb (40 kg) at 23 degrees; 55 lb at 55 degrees; 33 lb at 80 degrees
specs.Leg lock: Twist locks with knurled caps (Parallel Locking)
specs.Head: AirHed Pro ball head with twist clamp (in the kit version)
specs.Plate: QR Octa Arca-Swiss compatible plate, 1/4-20 screw

products.scoreNote: 88 lb rating, 55.5 in column-down height and tough carbon legs make it the most stable here; 24 in fold and 3.8 lb without the head cost portability.
products.amazonTitle: 3 Legged Thing Pro Range 2.0 Winston 2.0 Kit Carbon Fibre Tripod System - Adjustable Camera Tripod with 3 Counterfold Detachable Legs for Monopod Conversion (IE-RG44-9V3D) (Bronze)

praise: Tough carbon legs that resist scratches on sharp rock, with twist locks that are easy to grip in the cold
Holds a lot of weight steady; the monopod conversion and hook for ballast are handy
Held up through months of snow, cold, saltwater and sand in a long-term test
complaints: Heavy and large for travel; needs its carry case
Section couplings can fill with water when submerged
Ball head locking needed care, with close calls in one review

sources.title: Mike Stehlik: Jay and Winston 2.0 long-term review

ownerQuotes.quote: I bought the Winston 2.0 last summer and it's been a great tripod for me. It's built tough and seen some harsh country here in New Mexico and is holding up amazingly well.
the section couplings will leak water into the tubes when submerged in the water.
Damn it can hold a lot of weight steady! But it's still light enough to where I need to add some ballast for the wind around here.
even with the center column extended to about 60-70% in "field conditions," I did not notice any motion blur when reviewing the photos.
A little larger than I'd prefer for a travel tripod

products.weak: Maker search snippet showed the 3leggedthing.com page as 'Out of stock' for one search result; the Amazon listing (B082FB275T) is the Bronze colour of the Kit and I did not confirm stock or the current (not discontinued) colourway. A second Winston 2.0 ASIN (B0821K7H2W, legs only, Spanish-language title) was seen and not used. Weight is 3.8 lb per maker but DCW and others quote about 2.05 kg (4.5 lb); only maker figure used. Leg lock is described by the maker as knurled-cap locks (Parallel Locking); DPReview owner calls them twist-locks.
